content:
To determine if two energy levels can be clearly resolved, we use the energy-time uncertainty principle. The lifetime \(\tau\) of a state corresponds to an energy width \(\Gamma \approx \hbar / \tau\). Two levels are resolvable if their energy difference \(\Delta E\) is larger than the sum (or at least the larger) of their widths.

Given:
- \(\tau_1 = 10^{-9} \text{ s}\) → \(\Gamma_1 \approx \hbar / \tau_1\)
- \(\tau_2 = 10^{-8} \text{ s}\) → \(\Gamma_2 \approx \hbar / \tau_2\)

Using \(\hbar \approx 6.58 \times 10^{-16} \text{ eV·s}\):
- \(\Gamma_1 \approx 6.58 \times 10^{-16} / 10^{-9} = 6.58 \times 10^{-7} \text{ eV}\)
- \(\Gamma_2 \approx 6.58 \times 10^{-16} / 10^{-8} = 6.58 \times 10^{-8} \text{ eV}\)

The larger width is \(\sim 6.6 \times 10^{-7} \text{ eV}\). To clearly resolve the levels, \(\Delta E\) must be significantly greater than this width (typically \(\Delta E > \Gamma_1 + \Gamma_2 \approx 7.2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ eV}\)).

Evaluating the options:
- (A) \(10^{-8} \text{ eV}\) is too small.
- (B) \(10^{-4} \text{ eV}\) is much larger than \(10^{-6} \text{ eV}\), so the levels are clearly resolved.
- (C) \(10^{-11} \text{ eV}\) is far too small.
- (D) \(10^{-9} \text{ eV}\) is too small.

Answer: B
